subject: Economy
sub_topic: Stock exchanges — BSE, NSE, SEBI role

concepts.name: SEBI: Statutory Status, Composition, and Legal Powers
key_dimensions: Transition from non-statutory (1988) to statutory body via SEBI Act, 1992 — a common trap on 'established vs. given statutory status'
Quasi-legislative, quasi-judicial, and quasi-executive powers — overlap and limits of each
Composition: Chairperson, members from Finance Ministry, RBI, and independent members — appointment and removal process
SEBI's power to issue regulations vs. Parliament's power to amend the Act — hierarchy of norms

concepts.name: SEBI's Regulatory Jurisdiction: Scope and Boundaries
key_dimensions: Securities regulated by SEBI vs. commodities (erstwhile FMC, now SEBI post-2015 merger) — what falls inside and outside SEBI's ambit
Overlap with RBI: forex-linked securities, government securities, currency derivatives — who regulates what
SEBI vs. IRDAI vs. PFRDA: jurisdiction over insurance-linked and pension-linked investment products
Extra-territorial jurisdiction: SEBI's power over FPIs and overseas listed Indian companies

concepts.name: BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange): Historical Significance and Structure
key_dimensions: Asia's oldest stock exchange (1875) — significance as a landmark often tested in context questions
BSE's recognition under Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act (SCRA), 1956 — statutory basis of recognition
Demutualization of BSE (2005): shift from broker-owned to corporate structure — why it matters for governance
BSE's SENSEX as a benchmark index: composition (30 stocks), free-float methodology — often confused with NIFTY 50

concepts.name: NSE (National Stock Exchange): Institutional Origins and Significance
key_dimensions: NSE established in 1992 on recommendations of Pherwani Committee — institutional origin often tested
NSE as a demutualised exchange from inception — contrast with BSE's demutualization in 2005
Introduction of electronic screen-based trading in India — NSE's transformative role vs. BSE's open-outcry legacy
NIFTY 50 index: composition, free-float market capitalization methodology, and distinction from SENSEX

concepts.name: Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act (SCRA), 1956: Framework for Stock Exchanges
key_dimensions: SCRA as the foundational legislation for recognizing and regulating stock exchanges — predates SEBI Act
Definition of 'securities' under SCRA vs. SEBI Act — subtle differences and what instruments are included/excluded
Central Government's power to recognize stock exchanges under SCRA — delegation to SEBI post-1992
Listing requirements and delisting governed under SCRA read with SEBI regulations — layered legal framework

concepts.name: Primary vs. Secondary Market: Roles and Regulatory Distinctions
key_dimensions: Primary market: IPO, FPO, rights issue — SEBI's ICDR (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations govern these
Secondary market: trading of already-issued securities on exchanges — price discovery mechanism
SEBI's differential oversight: prospectus-based disclosure in primary market vs. continuous disclosure obligations in secondary market
Role of investment bankers/merchant bankers in primary market vs. brokers in secondary market — SEBI registration requirements for each

concepts.name: Dematerialization and Depositories: NSDL and CDSL
key_dimensions: Depositories Act, 1996 — legal basis; NSDL (1996) and CDSL (1999) as the only two depositories in India
Demat account vs. trading account vs. bank account — three-account system and common confusion among them
SEBI's oversight over depositories vs. the exchanges themselves — regulatory layering
Mandatory dematerialization for trading: phased implementation and its impact on reducing fraud/paper-based risks

concepts.name: Market Intermediaries: Registration, Regulation, and SEBI Oversight
key_dimensions: Categories of intermediaries: brokers, sub-brokers, merchant bankers, portfolio managers, investment advisers, credit rating agencies — each requiring SEBI registration
SEBI's power to suspend/cancel registration — quasi-judicial nature and appeal mechanism to SAT
Credit Rating Agencies (CRAs): SEBI regulation, conflict-of-interest issues, role in 2008 global crisis narrative
Investment Advisers vs. Portfolio Managers — a UPSC trap: fiduciary duty difference and fee structure regulation

concepts.name: Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT): Jurisdiction and Significance
key_dimensions: SAT established under SEBI Act, 1992 — appeals against SEBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA orders (multi-regulator appellate body — a key trap)
SAT composition: Presiding Officer (retired Supreme Court/High Court judge) and members
Appeal from SAT lies to Supreme Court directly — bypasses High Court (important procedural trap)
SAT's role in checking SEBI's quasi-judicial overreach — institutional check on regulator

concepts.name: Insider Trading: Definition, Prohibition, and SEBI Enforcement
key_dimensions: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 — updated framework replacing 1992 regulations
Definition of 'Unpublished Price Sensitive Information' (UPSI) — what qualifies and what does not (a trap in MCQs)
Trading window closure concept and 'connected persons' vs. 'insiders' — subtle definitional differences
SEBI's whistleblower mechanism and informant reward system introduced in 2019 amendments — recent development

concepts.name: Market Manipulation and SEBI's Enforcement Powers
key_dimensions: Types of manipulation: pump-and-dump, circular trading, spoofing, front-running — definitional distinctions
SEBI's power to order disgorgement of ill-gotten gains — not just penalty but asset recovery
SEBI's search and seizure powers (added via 2014 amendment) — expansion of investigative powers
Penalty structure under SEBI Act: Rs. 25 crore or 3 times the profit — whichever is higher (specific figure tested in exams)

concepts.name: IPO Regulatory Framework: SEBI ICDR Regulations
key_dimensions: Eligibility criteria for IPO: profitability track record vs. QIB route (for loss-making companies) — two tracks often confused
Book-building vs. fixed-price IPO mechanism — price discovery difference
Reservation for categories: QIBs (50%), NIIs (15%), RIIs (35%) — specific proportions are a frequent trap
ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount): mandatory mechanism, role of Self Certified Syndicate Banks (SCSBs)

concepts.name: Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) vs. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI): Regulatory Divide
key_dimensions: FPI regulated by SEBI; FDI regulated by DPIIT/RBI under FEMA — dual regulatory structure
FPI limit in Indian companies: sectoral caps and aggregate limits — SEBI vs. RBI role in monitoring
FPI to FDI reclassification trigger: when FPI holding crosses 10% in a listed company
P-Notes (Participatory Notes): SEBI regulations, anonymity concerns, KYC tightening — a recurring current-affairs topic

concepts.name: Mutual Funds: SEBI Regulation and Structural Framework
key_dimensions: Three-tier structure: Sponsor → Trust (AMC overseen by Trustees) — legal ownership vs. management distinction
SEBI's categorization and rationalization of mutual fund schemes (2017) — why SEBI mandated it and its impact
NAV calculation and its daily disclosure requirement — transparency obligation under SEBI
SEBI's recent regulations on total expense ratio (TER) caps and commission disclosure — investor protection angle

concepts.name: Bond Market and Debt Securities: SEBI's Role vs. RBI's Role
key_dimensions: Government securities (G-Secs) regulated by RBI; corporate bonds regulated by SEBI — the critical dividing line
SEBI's push for corporate bond market development: mandatory listing of debt securities above a threshold
Credit Default Swaps (CDS) on corporate bonds: jointly regulated by SEBI and RBI — overlap area
Municipal bonds and infrastructure investment trusts (InvITs) under SEBI regulation — newer instruments

concepts.name: Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and SEBI Regulation
key_dimensions: AIF categories: Category I (VCFs, SME funds, social venture), Category II (PE, debt funds), Category III (hedge funds) — differential regulatory treatment
AIFs as distinct from mutual funds and PMS — minimum investment thresholds and accredited investor concept
SEBI's concern about Category III AIFs being used for tax arbitrage and regulatory circumvention
Overseas investment by AIFs: SEBI and RBI/FEMA interplay — dual approval requirement

concepts.name: SEBI's Role in Corporate Governance: Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR)
key_dimensions: SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 — mandatory governance standards for listed companies (board composition, audit committee, related-party transactions)
Independent directors: SEBI's role vs. Companies Act, 2013 (MCA) — overlapping jurisdiction and a common trap
Stewardship Code for institutional investors — SEBI's expectation of active shareholder engagement
SEBI's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) mandate for top listed companies — ESG disclosure angle

concepts.name: T+1 Settlement Cycle: India's Global Leadership and Systemic Implications
key_dimensions: India as the first major market to implement T+1 settlement (fully by 2023) — ahead of the US which moved to T+1 in 2024
Settlement cycle evolution: T+5 → T+3 → T+2 → T+1 — each step's rationale (counterparty risk reduction)
Role of Clearing Corporations (NSE Clearing Ltd., BSE Clearing) in guaranteeing settlement — central counterparty concept
FPI concerns about T+1: currency hedging mismatch — SEBI's accommodation measures and debate

concepts.name: Financial Market Infrastructure: Clearing Corporations and Payment Systems Interface
key_dimensions: Clearing corporations as Central Counterparties (CCPs) — novation concept: how they eliminate bilateral counterparty risk
Interoperability of clearing corporations: SEBI's 2019 mandate for cross-exchange clearing — competition implications
Interface between stock market settlement and RBI's RTGS/NEFT — systemic risk considerations
Default waterfall mechanism in clearing corporations: margins → default fund → CCP's own capital — sequence is a potential trap

concepts.name: SEBI's Investor Protection Measures: Grievance Redressal and Financial Literacy
key_dimensions: SCORES (SEBI Complaints Redress System) — online complaint portal; timeline obligations for companies to respond
Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPEF) under SEBI — funded by unclaimed dividends and investor awareness mandate
SEBI's Investor Charter: a standardized disclosure document mandated for all intermediaries (2021) — recent initiative
Distinction between SEBI's SCORES and RBI's CRPC (Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre) — which handles which type of complaint (trap)
